prerequisites: No specific prior learning is required, apart from basic reading comprehension and fundamental mathematical knowledge.

learning_outcomes.text: Know and value the fundamental principles of business administration, and the framework in which it operates.
Deepen understanding of the management process and the different functions of the manager.
Understand the different alternatives for structuring a company.
Know performance evaluation processes and reward, incentive, and personal and professional development systems.
Study company direction and control as functions. Value the importance of studying modes of conduct and communication processes.
Approach relevant aspects of financial decisions in the company and their implication in business performance and investment project selection.
Verify the requirements of the marketing function and its relationship with product design, pricing, and distribution.
Know the most relevant aspects of the production management function.
Study key aspects of product development, the need for simultaneous engineering, and understand the importance of adequate product design for the process.
Know the different types of processes and their fundamental characteristics. Learn to make a correct process selection. Know the process representation technique.
Relate the optimal functioning of the production process to the adequacy of plant capacity, facilities, their location, and the distribution of equipment and plant facilities.
Know and apply production and project programming and control techniques, especially through computerized systems.

Know total quality techniques and interpret the importance of quality commitment and customer service. Value the importance of objective measurement and control as a feedback mechanism and efficiency guarantee.

Students must have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds upon general secondary education, and is typically found at a level that, while supported by advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects involving knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.

Students must be able to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional manner and possess the competencies typically demonstrated by the elaboration and defense of arguments and problem-solving within their field of study.
Adequate knowledge of the concept of a company, its institutional and legal framework. Business organization and management.
Ability to work in a multilingual and multidisciplinary environment.
Knowledge of basic and technological subjects, enabling them to learn new methods and theories, and providing them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Ability to handle specifications, regulations, and mandatory standards.
Ability to organize and plan in the field of business, and other institutions and organizations.

syllabus_topics: The company, its types, and its structure
Information and economic decisions in the company
Analysis and valuation of investment projects
Marketing in the company and commercial management
Operations and production management. Strategic aspects
Programming and control instruments for productive activities
Production and operations management. Tactical aspects
Digital transformation and innovation in the company
teaching_methods: Self-study of basic bibliography texts, recommended in sessions of at least 3 hours.
Analysis of practical cases from companies, professionals, and situations.
Review of provided examples and solved exercises.
Completion of self-assessment questions and summaries for each topic.
Optional completion of two continuous assessment activities (voluntary project, video creation).

assessment_methods.method: Preparation of videos demonstrating knowledge assimilation (especially practical exercises)

assessment_rules: The final exam is a multiple-choice test with 15 questions, 4 options per question, only one correct. Correct answers are worth 0.67 points, incorrect answers subtract 0.2 points, and unanswered questions score 0. To pass the exam, the total score (correct - incorrect) must be 5 or more. Students can optionally complete two continuous assessment activities (voluntary project, video preparation) which together can contribute up to 30% of the final grade, weighted with the on-site exam (70%), provided a minimum score of 4 (out of 10) is achieved on the exam. If the continuous assessment activities are not completed or if they lower the overall grade, only the exam score will be considered. Both continuous assessment activities must be completed for them to count. For an 'Honors' (Matrícula de Honor) distinction, both activities must be completed.
